summary: B is preferable because its out-of-scope retry change is substantially narrower and its upload retry test exercises an os.File and verifies identical multipart bodies. Both patches still violate the contract by implementing Upload through Raw.Do instead of FilesService.Add.
reasons: Both candidates correctly add the required Upload signature, use internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field "file", validate inputs, and preserve the public Add signature.

Neither routes Upload through FilesService.Add; both duplicate its option processing, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error handling, creating the exact maintenance divergence the contract forbids.

A eagerly buffers nearly every nonstandard io.Reader whenever WithNoRetry is absent, even when the configured policy would not retry the method. This can destroy streaming behavior, block on pipes before sending, and cause unbounded memory use across unrelated RawClient calls.

B limits its additional retry behavior to io.ReadSeeker bodies and explicitly preserves one-shot behavior for forward-only streams, making its scope violation materially smaller than A's global buffering change.V2 Upload's retry test uses an os.File, confirms two attempts after a 429, compares the complete encoded bodies, and inspects the multipart filename on retry. A's Upload retry test merely drains the bodies and counts attempts.V1 A does provide explicit source-reader-error and request-option tests, which B lacks, but this test advantage does not outweigh A's broad behavioral change.
risks_a: Global eager buffering changes RawClient, Files.Add, Files.Update, and unrelated streaming requests despite the contract prohibiting retry-machinery refactoring.
Large or unbounded readers can cause excessive memory use or prevent a request from starting.
Upload still bypasses Add and duplicates its behavior.
risks_b: Upload still bypasses Add and duplicates its behavior.
The custom GetBody closure reuses and seeks the same mutable reader instead of returning an independent body, which is less idiomatic and may be unsafe under overlapping body consumption.
It changes seekable Add/Update retry and close-ownership semantics contrary to the scope contract, and it omits the required source-reader-error test.
